description: Python For Nonprofits demonstrates how to use Python to retrieve, analyze, visualize, and share nonprofit data.

summary.one_liner: Python for Nonprofits is an MIT-licensed guide and collection of Jupyter notebooks teaching nonprofit staff to import, clean, analyze, visualize, and publish data with Python.
summary.what_it_does: The project walks through importing and reformatting data, then running descriptive statistics and linear regressions. It covers creating static charts and maps, including Plotly and Folium choropleth maps. It also shows how to share spreadsheets and interactive visualizations online, including static webpages and Dash apps. Most examples use simulated data from a fictional university (Northern Virginia Catholic University), with some real US Census data. The README describes it as a book-style resource meant to be read in order, with an HTML and PDF version built via Jupyter Book.
use_cases: learning python for nonprofit data analysis
cleaning and reformatting messy spreadsheet data
making charts and choropleth maps from census data
how_to_run: Open docs/index.html in a browser to read the HTML version of the book
Or open the Jupyter Notebooks one by one in the suggested order from the table of contents
Set render_for_pdf to False in Appendix/helper_funcs.py to get interactive HTML visuals when running locally
Install Python via Miniforge and libraries from conda-forge (some via pip)
notable: Organized as a book-style sequence from data import through Dash app publishing
Uses simulated data from a fictional university (NVCU) plus real US Census data
Includes both Plotly and Folium choropleth map tutorials
Provides a PDF book version and an HTML version built with Jupyter Book
Released under the MIT license, allowing commercial and personal reuse
caveats: Not a replacement for an introductory Python course; assumes basic Python background
Online HTML version of the book is not yet available; the HTML version must be run locally from the download
Some libraries may need to be installed via pip rather than conda-forge
